title: Trump declares an energy ceasefire
ticker: BREAKING: Trump declares an "ENERGY CEASEFIRE" between Russia and Ukraine
Kremlin: "Contacts are ongoing" - no confirmation from Moscow
Ukraine says Russia struck a power plant in Kharkiv after the announcement
Trump's diesel deal with Putin: 300,000 tons now, 500,000 in November

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Welcome to KOWEN News.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: President Trump says Russia and Ukraine have agreed to an *energy ceasefire*, effective immediately.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: But Moscow has *not confirmed it*, and Ukraine says it found out *from the media*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: Within hours, Kyiv reported a Russian strike on a *power plant in Kharkiv*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: We look at what Trump announced, what each side is saying, and why this deal is so closely tied to *diesel prices* in America.

scenes.name: Donald J. Trump
scenes.post: Effective immediately, there is an ENERGY CEASEFIRE in the War between Russia and Ukraine. Both parties have agreed. Do not break it!

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: It came in a short post on Truth Social on Sunday morning.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Effective immediately, Trump wrote, there is an *energy ceasefire* in the war between Russia and Ukraine.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Both parties have agreed. *Do not break it*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: That was the entire statement. No details on *what targets* are covered, *how long* it lasts, or *who would monitor* it.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The White House did not immediately answer requests for more information.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Here is where things stand. Trump says *both sides* signed on.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The Kremlin has *not confirmed* any agreement.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Ukraine says it supports the idea, but was *not told* in advance.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: And so far, nobody has published the *terms* of the deal.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: To understand why Trump wants this, you have to follow the *diesel*.

items.text: Trump: both sides agree "not to hit" energy

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: For weeks, Trump has pressed Zelensky to *stop striking Russian oil refineries*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He argues those strikes have cut *global diesel supplies* and pushed up fuel prices for Americans.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Diesel prices in the U.S. have hit *record highs* since the U.S. launched its war with Iran in February.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: On Friday, Trump struck a *diesel deal* with Vladimir Putin.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: On Saturday, after Zelensky criticized that deal, Trump said Ukraine should get *a new leader who can make a deal*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: And on Sunday came the *ceasefire post*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Kyiv says hitting Moscow's oil industry is a *legitimate strategy*, because oil money pays for *Russia's war*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Under Friday's deal, the U.S. agreed to lift sanctions on *Russian fuel*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Trump said Russia would *immediately* release three hundred thousand tons of diesel to the American and global market.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Then *five hundred thousand tons* in November, and another *million* after that.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The Treasury Department authorized *temporary sanctions relief* to make those shipments possible.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Ukrainian and European officials reacted with *dismay*, saying the money will help pay for *Russia's war*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Diesel moves trucks, tractors and freight trains, so its price shows up in *almost everything Americans buy*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Farmers, truckers and businesses that run *heavy equipment* are feeling it most.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: And with the *midterm elections* weeks away, fuel prices have become a major political issue.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Ukraine's refinery strikes hit Russian *fuel production and exports*. Stopping them could put *more Russian diesel* on the market.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: So how did Ukraine react? With a *yes*, but a cautious one.

scenes.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
scenes.quote: Ready to refrain from striking Russian energy infrastructure, and we count on the same readiness from Russia.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Zelensky said Ukraine *welcomed* the announcement, calling it *good news for everyone*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He said Ukraine is *ready to stop* striking Russian energy infrastructure, and counts on *the same readiness* from Russia.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He said Ukraine has proposed many steps to calm the war, but Putin had *one answer* to all of them. *Nyet*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He said Kyiv is staying in contact with Washington, and that he had discussed the news with Canada's Mark Carney, Finland's Alexander Stubb and NATO chief *Mark Rutte*.

scenes.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
scenes.quote: Don't attack us. Don't kill our children. We will stop attack your diesel.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Earlier on Sunday, in an interview with ABC News, Zelensky made his offer to Moscow very simple.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: *Don't attack us. Don't kill our children.* We will stop attack your diesel.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He also asked Trump to give the Kremlin *a signal* not to attack Ukraine's energy system.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Zelensky also pushed back on the idea that Ukraine is to blame for fuel prices.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Everybody in the world understands, he said, that prices are rising *because of the war in the Middle East*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Asked why Trump and Elon Musk blame him, he said it is *more difficult to stop Putin* than to pressure others.

scenes.name: Kharkiv
scenes.quote: Ukraine says Russia hit energy sites in Kyiv and Kharkiv after the ceasefire post.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: But on the ground, the attacks *did not stop*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Zelensky said Ukrainian skies were *full of Russian Shahed drones* all day, with glide bombs and strikes on energy infrastructure.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: A *power plant in Kharkiv* was attacked in the evening. His office confirmed it came *after* Trump's post.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Ukrainian officials reported more strikes on Monday morning, including on an *energy facility* on the outskirts of Kharkiv.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: A day earlier, a Russian bombing in *Zaporizhzhia* killed twenty three people, including *four children*, according to Zelensky.

scenes.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
scenes.quote: We didn't know about it. We learned from the media. This looks strange.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: On Monday, speaking at the Warsaw Security Forum, Zelensky went further.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: We *didn't know about it*. We learned from the media, he said.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: We do support it, but I have not heard approval from the Russian side, and *this looks strange*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: And what is Moscow saying? So far, *very little*.

scenes.name: Dmitry Peskov
scenes.quote: Contacts are ongoing. When we have anything to say on this topic, we'll be sure to keep you informed.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov would only say that *contacts are ongoing*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He would not say *who* those contacts are with, the U.S., Ukraine, or both.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: He also *declined to say* whether the ceasefire would cover only oil refineries.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In other words, Russia has *neither confirmed nor denied* that it agreed.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: This is not the first energy truce of this war.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: In March 2025, after a call with Trump, Putin agreed to a *30-day pause* on strikes against energy targets.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Just last month, on September fourteenth, Trump said both countries had agreed *not to hit* each other's energy infrastructure.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Moscow did not confirm that one either, and both sides *kept attacking* energy sites.

scenes.name: Winter is coming
scenes.quote: Ukrainian officials say Russia is "weaponizing winter" by targeting power, heat and water.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: For Ukraine, the stakes are high. Winter is weeks away.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Russia has spent the war trying to cut Ukrainian civilians off from *power, heat and running water*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Ukrainian officials call the strategy *weaponizing winter*.

scenes.name: Yandex data centers
scenes.quote: Three strikes on Yandex facilities in four days. Taxi, shopping and banking apps went down.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Ukraine, meanwhile, keeps hitting targets *deep inside Russia*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: On Sunday, a drone attack shut down a *Yandex data center* in the city of Vladimir, east of Moscow.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: It was the *third strike* on the tech giant's facilities in four days.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Users in dozens of Russian cities could *not order taxis* or reach *banking services*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Across the border, local officials said a Ukrainian drone strike in Russia's *Bryansk* region killed one man and wounded two women.

scenes.name: Volodymyr Zelensky
scenes.quote: Give us two months, 60 days off. Total ceasefire, 60 days, and we will organize elections.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Zelensky also answered Trump's call for a new leader.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Give us *60 days* of total ceasefire, he said, *and we will organize elections*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Ukraine has been under *martial law* since 2022, and its constitution bars elections while it is in force.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The Kremlin quickly *rejected* the 60-day idea, saying Russia wants a *lasting peace*, not a ceasefire.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: So what happens now? The key question is simple. *Does Russia say yes?*

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: The Trump administration has spent weeks trying to negotiate a *reciprocal halt* to energy attacks, as part of wider efforts to end the war.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: With the armies largely *deadlocked* on the front line, both sides have turned to a *long-range air war*, and energy is one of its main targets.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: If Moscow confirms, it would be the first *real pause* in the energy war in months.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: If it doesn't, this could go the way of September's announcement, *a truce on paper only*.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: Even if it holds, an energy ceasefire is *not a peace deal*. The fighting on the front line goes on.

lines.speaker: Reporter
lines.text: And nobody has said *how violations* would be tracked.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: An energy ceasefire *announced in Washington*, but not yet confirmed in Moscow.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: We'll keep following whether the strikes *actually stop*.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: If you found this helpful, please *like and subscribe* for more.

lines.speaker: Anchor
lines.text: This has been KOWEN News. Thanks for watching.
